newsitem.title: USA: UAL earnings trimmed by reservation system sale.
newsitem.headline: UAL earnings trimmed by reservation system sale.

text.p: The sale of a major stake in a computerized airline reservation system will hurt earnings for UAL Corp. this year, but the Chicago-based parent of United Airlines said Wednesday it expects to make up the shortfall with stronger-than-expected air carrier operations.

Analysts applauded United's sale of its 77 percent stake in Apollo Travel Services to electronic airline reservation company Galileo International Partnership for $539 million, saying it raises cash that the airline can use to reduce debt or buy aircraft.
UAL stock was up 25 cents to $80.125 in the afternoon on the New York Stock Exchange.

Galileo, which has headquarters in Rosemont, Ill., is owned by 11 airlines. United holds a 38 percent stake in Galileo. Apollo is the exclusive distributor in the United States for Galileo's airline reservation system.

UAL declined to quantify the expected loss of earnings from the pending sale, but Goldman Sachs analyst Glenn Engel said he estimated the Galileo deal could cut UAL earnings by 20 cents to 25 cents a share in 1997.
UAL earned $1.01 billion, or $7.68 share, before extraordinary items in 1996.
"United ... will make up for (dilution from the deal) on operations. The airline business continues better than expected," Engel said.
The sale of United's stake in Apollo was part of an intricate deal announced late Tuesday.
Galileo will buy Apollo from three airlines, including United, for a total of $700 million. US Airways owns 21 percent of Apollo and Air Canada holds another 2 percent.

Galileo also plans to buy the Dutch and Swiss marketing companies for its services, Galileo Nederland B.V. and Traviswiss, which are owned by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV and Swissair AG, respectively.

While Galileo plans to fund its acquisitions with an initial public offering, United said it will not sell any of its Galileo shares in the offering and plans to have a significant stake in Galileo in the future.
Galileo provides travel agencies and other subscribers with the ability to access airline schedule and fare information, book reservations and issue tickets for 525 airlines.
